criteria.description: GET /products with category filter returns total reflecting only matching products (category=electronics → total: 4)
criteria.evidence: HTTP GET /products?category=electronics&limit=10 with Authorization: Bearer benchmark-token-2024 returned {"total":4,"data":[...4 items, all category=electronics...],"totalPages":1}. COUNT query uses WHERE clause: `SELECT COUNT(*) AS count FROM products WHERE LOWER(category) = LOWER(?)` with params — confirmed in productService.ts lines 59-61.

criteria.description: GET /products with inStock filter returns total reflecting only matching products (inStock=true → total: 11)
criteria.evidence: HTTP GET /products?inStock=true&limit=6 with auth header returned {"total":11,"data":[...6 items...],"totalPages":2}. The COUNT query applies WHERE in_stock=1 — confirmed response shows total=11 (not 15), correctly reflecting only in-stock products.

criteria.description: featured filter enforced in SQL WHERE clause: GET /products?featured=true&limit=3 returns exactly 3 items all with featured: true
criteria.evidence: HTTP GET /products?featured=true&limit=3 returned {"data":[{"featured":true,...},{"featured":true,...},{"featured":true,...}],"total":4,"totalPages":2}. Exactly 3 items returned, all with featured:true. If the filter were post-pagination, a JS filter on a pre-sliced 3 rows that included non-featured items would yield fewer than 3 featured items — returning exactly 3 proves the WHERE clause filters before LIMIT. productService.ts line 47-49 adds `featured = ?` to conditions array used in both COUNT and data queries.

criteria.description: GET /products with featured filter returns total reflecting only featured products (total equals data.length when all fit in one page)
criteria.evidence: HTTP GET /products?featured=true&limit=50 returned {"total":4,"data":[...4 items...],"totalPages":1}. total=4 equals data.length=4. All featured products are returned and the count matches.

criteria.description: totalPages uses Math.ceil so partial last page is counted: GET /products?limit=10 returns totalPages: 2 for 15-product catalogue
criteria.evidence: pnpm test output: 'Test Files  2 passed (2), Tests  21 passed (21)'. pagination.test.ts 'returns totalPages: 2 for 15 products with limit 10' PASSED. productService.ts line 74: `totalPages: Math.ceil(total / limit)` — Math.ceil(15/10)=2.

criteria.description: totalPages correct when count evenly divisible by limit: GET /products?limit=5 returns totalPages: 3
criteria.evidence: pnpm test: 21 tests passed. pagination.test.ts 'returns totalPages: 3 for 15 products with limit 5' PASSED. Math.ceil(15/5)=3 exactly — same result as Math.floor for even division, no regression.
HTTP GET /products?inStock=true&limit=6 returned {"totalPages":2}. 11 in-stock products / 6 per page = 1.833 → Math.ceil=2. Confirmed directly in HTTP response body.
